sections.html:
Three paths lead to a sale here: list with an agent, sell privately, or hand the house over to a cash buyer as it stands. Cash fits an owner who cannot sit through showings, loan approvals and inspection demands. What you give up is the premium a polished listing might earn.

Maple Valley is a family suburb southeast of Seattle with 28,482 estimated residents as of July 1, 2025. About 83 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $724,700. Households average about 3.01 people and earn a median of $152,885. With numbers like these, judge each offer by what you keep. A quick checklist:

  • Payoff amounts for your mortgage and any second loan or lien.
  • Repairs an inspector or buyer is likely to put on the table.
  • Commission and excise tax on a listing versus the cost of a direct deal.
  • The number of months you can afford the payments while the house sits.

Tenants matter too. A renter about to leave, or a lease that outlasts your target date, can settle which path works.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,984 a month, and the median rent is $2,304. The average commute is 37 minutes, which is long, so lead with how quickly your house reaches State Route 169, State Route 18 and State Route 516.

Lake Wilderness, Lake Lucerne, Rock Creek and a piece of Pipe Lake lie inside city limits. Rain falls harder here than in Seattle, so walk the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl space yourself before an inspector does.

On or near water? Economic and Community Development wants a call before you cut trees (lakefront lots especially), alter wetlands, slopes or streams, or build or replace a dock. Clear up any question about earlier work with the city before listing day.

sections.h2: When a house needs a permit
sections.html:
The city's Economic and Community Development Department, (425) 413-8800, answers permit questions. Common projects sort out like this:

ProjectBuilding permit
New structure or additionRequired
Installing or replacing windowsRequired
Remodel that moves structural members, plumbing or mechanical fixturesRequired
Fence over 6 feetRequired
Storage building under 200 square feetNot required, setbacks apply
Siding replacement, painting, flooringNot required
Fence under 6 feetNot required

Sale time is when gaps show. On a multiple listing service sale, you disclose improvements and repairs and say whether permits and inspections were obtained. Many lenders refuse to finance without a final inspection on record, and a home with unpermitted changes can face tear-down, vacating or costly repairs. Unsure about your parcel? Ask the department before listing.

sections.h2: Can you add units on your lot?
sections.html:
Often, yes. State law E2SHB 1110 makes cities of Maple Valley's size allow middle housing on lots zoned mostly residential, and the city's FAQ applies it to the R-4 and R-6 single-family zones. Duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhouses, stacked flats, courtyard apartments and cottage housing are all on the menu. A lot with a single-family home may add two accessory dwelling units, three units in all.

Buyers who smell development potential will study lot size and zoning, so get the department's answer on what your parcel allows before calling it a development site.

Most sellers of improved residential property must deliver a disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020 within five business days of a written contract that both sides accepted, unless they set a different schedule. The buyer's right to rescind lasts three business days.

Excise tax is normally the seller's bill, due to the county treasurer on the sale date. A graduated state rate applies, plus a local rate. Closings from January 1, 2027 use bands starting at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000 and rates of 1.1, 1.28, 2.75 and 3 percent from bottom to top. Earlier closings use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. A sale at the city median is taxed partly at 1.1 percent and partly at 1.28 percent.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and value appeals
sections.html:
King County sends the bill, and the schedule comes from RCW 84.56.020: pay by April 30, or pay half then and the remainder by October 31. Late taxes on residential property with four or fewer units accrue 9 percent a year in interest and no penalties. Statements go out by March 15 when budgets and rolls are ready.

RCW 84.40.038 governs value disputes. File with the county board of equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the notice (up to 60 if the county chose a longer window), whichever is later. For good cause such as serious illness or a natural disaster, the board may accept a late filing. Read the notice for your exact deadline, and call the King County Assessor or Treasury Operations about your account.

The title company typically prorates the current bill at closing.

sections.h2: Offer to closing in four steps
sections.html:
1. Collect payoff letters, your latest tax statement and permit records.
  2. Finish the disclosure statement and deliver it within five business days of acceptance.
  3. Accept the offer in writing so the title company can draft a settlement statement.
  4. Pay excise tax out of proceeds and sign the deed.

A cash deal drops showings, buyer financing and most inspection haggling, so it can close faster. A listing takes longer but may pay more when the house shows clean.

sections.h2: Papers to have ready before you list
sections.html:
Buyers and their lenders in Maple Valley tend to ask for the same few records, and having them in a folder saves days. Bring your deed, the latest King County tax statement and any payoff letters. Add permit records for windows, additions and remodels, since those are the projects the city flags. If the lot touches a lake, creek or wetland, include whatever correspondence you have with Economic and Community Development about trees, docks or slopes.

Walk through the house with the disclosure form in hand and answer every line from what you know. Where the answer is yes, attach a short explanation rather than leaving it blank. A complete form shortens the back and forth once an offer is in.

Set each offer against what a listing would realistically deliver. Take the list price, subtract commission, excise tax, repair credits and holding costs, then subtract your payoff on both sides. Get the closing date and the costs the buyer expects you to cover in writing, and let a title company or attorney read the contract.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Maple Valley?
faqs.a: Yes, new or replacement windows need a building permit. Siding replacement and painting do not. When in doubt, call Economic and Community Development at (425) 413-8800.

faqs.q: What happens if past work on my Maple Valley house had no permit?
faqs.a: Expect friction. Unpermitted changes can mean tear-down, vacating or costly repairs, and many lenders want proof of a final inspection. You also have to disclose improvements and whether permits were pulled, so ask the city what it has on file.

faqs.q: Can I add accessory dwelling units on a Maple Valley lot?
faqs.a: Often. A lot with a single-family home may add two ADUs, giving three units total, under the middle housing rules that follow state law HB 1110. Confirm your zoning and lot details with the city first.

faqs.q: When are Maple Valley property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the full amount, or half by then and the second half by October 31 under RCW 84.56.020. King County sends the bill. Delinquent taxes on residential property with four or fewer units accrue 9 percent annual interest.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my assessed value in Maple Valley?
faqs.a: Petition the county board of equalization by July 1 or within the days stated on your value notice, whichever is later. RCW 84.40.038 allows 30 days, or up to 60 if the county picked that. Bring evidence of value.
